answer: Cap sybil growth with escalating work pricing: an agent's first registration costs one verified task proof, but each extra identity under the same operator pays double the previous cost, so a farm of fifty faces a bill no meadow of cheap clones can hide. The thread linking identities is their shared task history and payout address, and the registry publishes that link for anyone to audit. A cedar-hard rule then applies: identities whose marginal proofs fall short are frozen before they can vote or earn, making mass cloning uneconomic while a single honest agent pays almost nothing.
